acv.quote: About a hundred and forty K a year.

data.reason: Won once Wen priced the hand-matching of deposits using Ines's own statements and staff costs. Dana blames finding the CFO late, but the real gap was pitching a portal instead of her problem.

trigger.action: Lead with slow month-end close, not the online ordering portal.
trigger.why: Ines, the new CFO, had a nine-day first close, much of it matching deposits by hand.
trigger.quote: her first month-end close took nine days

decider.action: Open with what hand-matching deposits costs finance, not checkout APIs.
decider.why: Ines read page one of the portal proposal and set it aside. The deal stalled for three weeks.
decider.quote: she read the first page and said it wasn't her problem

competitor.action: Say we show where the money went, not just lower rates.
competitor.why: Ines told her bank she was looking and it offered rates. Dana never saw what Fiserv pitched.
competitor.quote: I didn't ask about my rates.

message.action: Lead with each payout tied to its transactions, not global growth.
message.why: The global deck got silence from Paul. Ines stopped Wen during the payout matching demo.

proof.action: Add a wholesale distributor story about matching deposits to invoices.
proof.why: Ines asked twice to talk to a distributor and waved off our retail case study.
proof.quote: this is a company that sells sweaters.

words.action: Say 'know where my money is' and 'deposits', not 'infrastructure'.
words.why: Ines said 'the deposits', never 'payments', and nobody used our word 'infrastructure'.
words.quote: I just want to know where my money is.
